findings.claim: The RootControlJournal ceiling recurrence omits the per-attempt root debit required by Section 6.3: the append protocol debits one attempt plus worst-case overhead from the finite administrative_recovery allocation, but the only Section 7.1 root recurrence subtracts ΣO_root_j, where O_root_j is defined as root append overhead and root records have no root-attempt-unit field. Root attempts are therefore undercounted (or ambiguously folded into overhead), so repeated failed/UNKNOWN administrative attempts are not mechanically bounded by C_root.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Root units are debited only from `C_root`; administrative/operation units only from `C`. ... each root append appears in exactly one `O_root_j` and decrements `root_remaining_units := C_root - ΣO_root_j`.
findings.impact: Administrative append/recovery can exceed the HUMAN-bound root ceiling while still appearing reconciled, breaking the no-double-debit/ceiling invariant and making post-charge fail-stop accounting and P3/P15 admission evidence unsound.
findings.recommended_action: Define explicit root operation-unit and overhead fields and a recurrence that debits each root authorization/commit/outcome/recovery append exactly once under C_root; state whether overhead includes the attempt unit, then synchronize P3/P15, matrix, handoff, and arithmetic fixtures.

findings.claim: The design introduces administrative recovery states `RESTORED_BLOCKED` and terminal `ADMIN_LEDGER_UNRECOVERABLE`, but they are not represented as edges/states in the normative composed transition table, nor explicitly admitted by the P3 allowlist or P15 capability manifest; the failure matrix has only a generic administrative-append row. Thus the administrative failure path is not mechanically closed across state, P3, P15, and matrix, leaving terminal disposition/re-entry rules dependent on prose rather than a single checkable contract.
findings.evidence_excerpt: `RESTORED_BLOCKED` cannot resume until the restored ledger appends a recovery-lineage entry carrying all failed/UNKNOWN debits; terminal `ADMIN_LEDGER_UNRECOVERABLE`.
findings.impact: A validator or handoff implementer can omit, misclassify, or incorrectly reopen these administrative terminal/recovery states; this risks recovery deadlock or an unbound path back toward admission after ledger evidence is unrecoverable.
findings.recommended_action: Add explicit administrative genesis/append/recovery terminal rows to the normative state table and failure matrix, name their P3/P15 acceptance/rejection rules and exact owner/effects, and add passing/failing fixtures plus handoff manifest cells.
